subject: Post-call: Meridian resilience priorities & ops checklist
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@meridiancap.com>
Cc: Tom Everett <tom.everett@meridiancap.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Meridian resilience priorities & ops checklist

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth after a fairly tactical conversation. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you called out
- Recent multi-hour degradation during peak reporting windows (late EOD batch, 11–12 PM ET); retries amplified load and increased tail latency.
- Lack of transparent per-route cost/latency breakdowns across models (hard to prioritize mitigation).
- Regulatory need to keep customer inference traffic within US regions; replication to EU only for analytics is allowed.

Current stack (as described)
- Inference: in-house endpoints on k8s + mixed GPU fleet (16GB + 48GB).
- Caching: basic HTTP edge cache for responses; no KV cache for model KV.
- Observability: Datadog for infra; limited token-level tracing in application.

Success criteria (what Meridian would call a win)
1) Maintain 99.95% availability for core payment-verification route during reporting window.
2) 95th percentile latency under 450ms for customer-facing prompts at 2x current steady QPS.
3) Clear rollback/fallback behavior so we never return errors for customer-facing flows — degrade to smaller model variant or local deterministic rulebook.

Incident history notes we captured
- Dec 2026: degraded 3.5 hrs; primary cause: autoscaler oscillation + cold KV cache misses.
- Jan 2027: transient spike after release; fallback failed due to incompatible model variant causing retries.

Redwood first-pass recommendations (subject to your ops/SEC review)
- Prefix/KV caching for the verification flow to cut repeated token work.
- Configure policy-based routing: route non-critical analytic requests to lower-cost region/variant; keep payment verification pinned to US-Dedicated cluster.
- Introduce a graceful-degradation policy: when autoscale cannot keep up, fallback to a quantized 7B model variant with deterministic post-processing rules to preserve correctness.
- Add token-level tracing on the verification route to correlate latency spikes to specific prompt shapes.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix (slo-matrix.xlsx) and a compact ops checklist (ops-checklist.pdf) showing the rollout sequence we discussed. Also included a short snippet file with example runbook entries (redwood-runbook-snippets.txt).

Proposed next steps
- Action 1: Meridian to share a sanitized incident log for Dec/Jan (time windows, request IDs) — Erin, can you confirm by EOD Thu?
- Action 2: Redwood to produce a 2-week proof-of-concept plan for the verification route (prefix caching + fallback) and an estimated cost delta. We aim to have a draft by Mar 16.
- Action 3: Schedule a 60-min ops deep-dive with your SREs — proposed slots next week: Wed 3/9 or Thu 3/10.

If that all looks good I'll schedule the deep-dive and share the PoC plan draft in HubSpot + a short read-only drive folder.

Thanks — appreciate the candid session.

—
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@meridiancap.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Everett <tom.everett@meridiancap.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Meridian resilience priorities & ops checklist

Thanks Laura — this is a good summary. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Incident data: we can share sanitized request IDs and a high-level error breakdown (5xx vs timeouts) but not full payloads; will upload to the HubSpot drive link you provided. ETA: Thu EOD PST.
- Availability target: our internal bar for the verification route is 99.99% but we agreed with product that 99.95% would be an initial objective while we validate fallback correctness.
- Fallback behavior: the January incident failed because the secondary model did not have the same deterministic post-processing steps (we trimmed punctuation in pre-processing). Any PoC must include a validation harness for outputs at low latency.

Also flagged that our security team will need a short note about data residency for the US-dedicated cluster — Tom, I’ll loop SEC-ops in a separate thread.

On scheduling: Wed 3/9 morning PT works for us.

Erin
VP, Platform Engineering | Meridian Capital
erin.walsh@meridiancap.com | +1 (212) 555-0987
